scope: Nemesis original basic-board standard semi-cooperative core; six original characters. SG01–SG04 only.

method.read_boundary: Read only the manifest and its seven listed source files. No browsing, summaries, questions, answer keys, reader material, prior audits, or source-discovery assessments were consulted. No reader communication.
method.page_reference_convention: Foreign-language references are physical PDF page numbers and printed page numbers, which coincide. English references use the manual sections/page mapping corroborated by the extraction table of contents and internal page cross-references; the English PDF was not allowed or inspected. Short quotations normalize line wrapping and discretionary line-break hyphenation.
method.quotation_policy: Verbatim excerpts are limited to at most 25 words per manual across this report. Other evidence is paraphrased and retains printed-page references. Short excerpt translations are explanatory, not additional source quotations.

authority_and_applicability.finding: All three 28-page PDFs are credible localized original Nemesis core manuals, applicable to the requested standard board and six characters. They are not Retaliation/Lockdown or expansion manuals.

evidence.paraphrase: 6 characters (Captain, Pilot, Scientist, Scout, Soldier, Mechanic).
The same six core characters.
The same six core characters.
Place the board basic side up.
Use the standard side, as illustrated.
Place the board standard side up in the middle of the table.
Polish translation: Monika Żabicka.
French translation: Antoine Prono.
Translation and editing: Sebastian Wenzlaff.

authority_and_applicability.additional_checks: All contain Adam Kwapiński authorship and Awaken Realms branding, original rules/development credits, the original Intruder composition (8 Adults/Jäger), standard setup on p6, and separate variants on p27. PDF production creation dates are February/March 2019, with modifications on 2019-10-15.
authority_and_applicability.limits: PDF metadata dates establish production metadata, not rules-version precedence. No explicit revision number or statement that one localization supersedes another was found. The manifest contains paths and hashes but no retrieval URLs/HTTP metadata; publisher-hosted provenance is supplied in the assignment, not independently provable from the allowed files. All hashes match. In particular Polish is explicitly credited as a translation, so its language is not evidence of an authoritative source-text hierarchy.

cases.case: All eight Adult miniatures are in Combat when another Adult must be placed.

evidence.paraphrase: Only Adults outside Combat are removed; their corresponding tokens return to the bag where possible.
After that removal procedure, the encounter Room receives an Adult miniature.
Remove from the board all Adults not engaged in Combat.
Then the player places an Adult miniature in the Room where the Encounter occurred.
Remove all Adult miniatures that are not in Combat.
evidence.exact_short_excerpt: qui ne sont pas en combat

evidence.paraphrase: Then place an Adult miniature in the Room where you must resolve an Encounter.
Take all Jäger [the localized Adult type] that are not in Combat off the board.
Then place a Jäger in the Room where the Encounter was triggered.

cases.express_rules: All four trigger the retreat procedure when all eight Adults are on the board, remove only those not in Combat, return their corresponding tokens if possible, and then instruct placement. All eight being in Combat leaves zero removable miniatures.
cases.inference_limits: No text specifies cancellation, a substitute marker, taking an Adult out of Combat, selecting a different type, or any other way to complete placement in this exact state. The parenthetical if possible concerns token return, not an explicit all-in-Combat placement rule. The general introductory Adults retreat wording is narrowed by the next explicit non-Combat removal instruction.
cases.conclusion: The foreign manuals repeat the gap; none uniquely resolves this edge case.

cases.case: Queen-development Egg after Nest has been marked destroyed, including destroyed-marker and objective persistence/reset.

evidence.paraphrase: The Queen development branch adds one Egg to the Intruder board if the Nest has no characters or remains undiscovered.
If there are no characters in the Nest (or its location has not yet been discovered), add another Egg to the Intruder board.
If the Nest has not yet been discovered or nobody is there, add an additional Egg token to the Intruder board.
If no character is in the Nest (or it has not yet been discovered), place 1 Xeno Egg on the Xeno board.
When no Eggs remain in the Nest (all have been taken or destroyed), the Nest is considered destroyed.
Place 1 damage marker on the Nest tile; it represents its destruction.
When no Eggs remain in the Nest (all carried elsewhere or destroyed), it is considered destroyed: place a Damage marker on it.
As soon as no Eggs remain in the Nest (all carried away or destroyed), the Nest counts as destroyed.
Place a Damage marker on the Nest to indicate that.
The Nest is destroyed when there is no Intruder Egg left in it.
The Nest is destroyed as soon as no Xeno Egg remains there.
[At final objective check,] verify that it meets the stated conditions.

cases.express_rules: The Queen development branch depends on character presence, not on Nest destroyed status, and contains no destroyed-Nest exception. The Intruder-board Eggs represent the Nest Eggs. Emptying the Nest makes it considered destroyed and places a marker. Objectives are checked at game end.
cases.partial_resolution: On the literal printed Queen rule, add the Egg when the no-character branch applies, even if a destruction marker was previously placed. None of these texts explicitly authorizes suppressing that Egg.
cases.inference_limits: The manuals do not say whether destruction is a permanent achieved event or a state to be reevaluated after Egg addition. They never instruct removing the destroyed marker on Egg replenishment, never exempt a destroyed Nest from Queen Egg addition, and never say a previously achieved destruction objective remains fulfilled despite new Nest Eggs. Temporal words when/as soon as do not alone settle permanence. Neither marker persistence by silence nor current Egg-count reevaluation can be promoted into an express objective ruling.
cases.conclusion: Egg placement is textually supported, but the requested combined state/objective case remains unresolved.

cases.case: Contamination on a SUCCESSFUL melee attack against an uncarried Egg.
cases.resolved_answer: Apply the normal one-card contamination draw. The printed Egg exception is conditioned on a miss; it does not remove that draw on a successful attack.

evidence.paraphrase: Melee step 1 adds one Contamination card to the Action discard pile.
The Combat die is rolled at step 3.
Egg attacks use the ordinary shooting or melee procedure.
For melee Egg attacks, missing is connected to the instruction granting no Contamination card and no Wounds.
Draw 1 Contamination card and add it to your discarded Action cards.
Roll the Combat die.

evidence.note: The initial if-condition scopes both negative predicates, joined by nor. No successful-hit exemption is stated.
evidence.paraphrase: If the character misses during melee, they neither draw a Contamination card nor suffer Serious Wounds.
evidence.exact_short_excerpt: Jeśli postać chybi podczas walki wręcz
evidence.excerpt_translation: If the character misses during melee

evidence.paraphrase: Draw a Contamination card and add it to your Action-card discard pile.
Roll a Combat die.

evidence.note: The fronted in-case-of-failure condition expressly conditions both no-Wound and no-card instructions. The failure refers to the attack, not a successful hit.
evidence.paraphrase: In the event of failure on a melee action, you suffer no Wound and must not draw a Contamination card.
Draw a Contamination card and place it on your discard pile.
Roll a Combat die and resolve its result.

evidence.note: German places the if-you-miss condition after the coordinated predicates, unlike the unambiguous fronted conditions in PL/FR. Its natural wide-scope reading conditions the whole conjunction; a narrower attachment to the nearest wound predicate is grammatically conceivable. The sentence does not explicitly say even on a hit or otherwise state a blanket exemption.
evidence.paraphrase: In the case of a melee action you need not draw a Contamination card and suffer no Wounds, if you miss.

cases.express_rules: The Egg action uses the melee action procedure, whose first step draws a card before target selection and the Combat roll. Polish and French expressly condition the no-card/no-Wound exception on a miss. Successful melee therefore has the normal draw and destroys an Egg for each damage, followed by the Egg rule’s Noise roll.
cases.independent_language_assessment: PL and FR independently remove the English trailing-condition attachment doubt: neither supports extending the miss exception to hits. DE retains trailing-condition attachment ambiguity and does not independently offer an unambiguous successful-hit exemption. Reading DE as a blanket no-card rule would require choosing the narrower attachment over the normal wide-scope reading and disregarding the explicit miss-conditioned PL/FR wording. No new rule or override is necessary to retain the ordinary draw on a hit.
cases.inference_limits: This adjudication is only for a successful attack. It does not repair the procedural inconsistency between a pre-roll draw and a miss-conditioned no-draw instruction. No refund, delayed draw, or other timing patch is specified, and none is inferred. A summary may safely state successful melee still draws the normal card; it should not invent a procedure for a miss or state that all Egg melee is contamination-free.
cases.conclusion: A narrow successful-attack update is supported by the general procedure and explicit Polish/French conditional exception. The foreign sources do not authorize a blanket exemption.
cases.english_summary_sufficiency: Sufficient for this narrowly specified successful-hit branch: the English normal procedure already draws the card, and the stated special exception concerns missing. Polish and French corroborate that scope instead of supplying a replacement rule. No language is being declared superior. The German trailing condition is less explicit, but does not expressly establish a contrary successful-hit exemption. If an English summary wishes to cover the miss procedure too, these sources do not resolve the pre-roll timing contradiction.

cases.case: A later character death after the first death unlocked Pods and a player subsequently relocked them.

evidence.paraphrase: The emergency procedure is triggered by the first character death.
Pods can subsequently be locked and unlocked through ordinary means.
The Pod section describes automatic unlocking on a death of any character during play.
evidence.exact_short_excerpt: when any Character dies during the game

evidence.paraphrase: When the first character (of any player) dies.
For the rest of the game they may be closed and opened normally.

evidence.note: The indefinite possessive refers to an unspecified member of the characters, not specifically the first. It supplies no explicit first-only restriction.
evidence.paraphrase: The Pods can also open automatically at the moment of the death of some/any character.
The ship AI launches emergency procedures when the first character is killed.
The Pods can be locked (and unlocked) again for the remainder of the game.

evidence.note: This is expressly first-time, replacing the English p26 any-character wording.
evidence.paraphrase: The first time a character dies.
evidence.exact_short_excerpt: La première fois qu’un personnage meurt
evidence.excerpt_translation: The first time a character dies

evidence.paraphrase: As soon as the first character dies (regardless of whose).
For the rest of the game the Pods may be locked and unlocked without restriction.

evidence.note: Explicit first-character restriction; no any-death wording here.
evidence.paraphrase: as soon as the first character dies.
evidence.excerpt_translation: as soon as the first character dies

evidence.paraphrase: The first time a character is killed, all Pods are automatically unlocked.
As soon as the first character dies (regardless of whose), all Pods are automatically unlocked.

language_verdicts.FR: resolved within this manual: death-triggered automatic unlocking is first death only, so the specified later death does not itself unlock relocked Pods.
language_verdicts.DE: resolved within this manual: first death only; the specified later death does not itself unlock relocked Pods.
language_verdicts.PL: unresolved internal broad-versus-first wording: p12/p28 specify first; p26 refers to death of an unspecified character and cross-refers p12.
language_verdicts.EN: unresolved internal conflict: p12/p28 first death; p26 any Character dies.

cases.express_rules: FR and DE consistently use first death in both the main critical-moment rule and Pod section, with re-locking allowed afterward. PL and EN have first-death main rules but broader Pod-section language.
cases.inference_limits: The French and German manuals are positive primary evidence for first-only intent and are clearer than the English and Polish Pod paragraphs. However, the allowed files provide no statement that FR/DE p26 correct or supersede EN/PL p26, no cross-language precedence, and no erratum. Selecting the clearer localizations as controlling the English summary would be an editorial choice rather than a universally unambiguous source instruction. Specific-over-general is not expressly stated here and does not itself eliminate the discrepancy.
cases.conclusion: New sources uniquely resolve the case within FR/DE, but do not eliminate the corpus conflict sufficiently to present a single unqualified English-core ruling as source-certain.
cases.english_summary_sufficiency: Insufficient for an unqualified English summary ruling. FR/DE each settle their own text, but transferring their correction of the Pod paragraph into the inconsistent English text would require an unsupported precedence or editorial-repair assumption.

overall.qualified_new_evidence: SG02 explicitly supports the added Queen Egg without resolving destruction/objective persistence. SG04 has materially clearer first-only wording in FR and DE, but EN/PL remain inconsistent and authority precedence is unestablished.
overall.no_house_rules: No substitute miniature, destruction reset/permanence rule, contamination refund/delay, blanket Egg exemption, or language-authority hierarchy is supplied or invented.
